annotations.title: ring + positivity replaces nlinarith hints
annotations.body: The pattern `have key : B - A = E^2 := by ring; rw [key]; positivity` eliminates the need for `nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a-b)]`. ring verifies the algebraic identity; positivity recognizes perfect squares automatically.
annotations.mathContext: For HM ≤ GM: $ab(a+b)^2 - (2ab)^2 = ab(a-b)^2$. Since $a,b>0$ and $(a-b)^2\geq 0$, the product $ab(a-b)^2 \geq 0$ is handled by positivity.

annotations.title: The canonical ring+positivity pattern
annotations.body: For GM ≤ AM: suffices h : 0 ≤ ((a+b)/2)^2 - a*b by linarith, then have key : ... = ((a-b)/2)^2 := by ring, then rw [key]; positivity. No manual witness needed.

annotations.title: polyrith not applicable to inequality goals
annotations.body: polyrith proves polynomial equalities (via Groebner basis / linear algebra over ℚ). For inequality goals like A ≤ B, it cannot be applied directly. positivity is the right tool after ring normalization.
annotations.mathContext: polyrith would prove e.g. $4a^2b^2 + a b(a-b)^2 = ab(a+b)^2$, but cannot conclude $4a^2b^2 \leq ab(a+b)^2$ directly.

annotations.title: suffices + linarith bridge
annotations.body: The `suffices h : 0 ≤ B - A by linarith` pattern converts A ≤ B into a nonnegativity goal, making positivity applicable. linarith then closes the original goal from h trivially.
annotations.mathContext: $A \leq B$ iff $0 \leq B - A$. This bridge is the key step enabling positivity automation.

annotations.title: HM ≤ GM requires degree-4 witness
annotations.body: The HM ≤ GM step requires the degree-4 identity ab(a+b)^2 - (2ab)^2 = ab(a-b)^2. This is why nlinarith [] (no hints) may fail here — it needs to search at degree 4 for the Positivstellensatz certificate, which exceeds nlinarith's default search depth.
annotations.mathContext: $4a^2b^2 \leq ab(a+b)^2$. Equivalently $0 \leq ab(a-b)^2 = (ab)^{1/2} \cdot ab^{1/2}(a-b)^2$ — a degree-4 SOS not directly recognized by nlinarith at default settings.
